payload.name: Resolve-relative-time-in-extraction
payload.description: When extracting candidate memories from a message, if the message contains a relative time expression ('last year', 'yesterday', 'last week') and the message timestamp is available, resolve it to an absolute date and include it in the candidate before CRUD.
content: During extraction, for every statement about a past event that includes a relative time reference, convert that reference to an absolute date using the message's timestamp (e.g., 'last year' on 1 Dec 2023 -> 2022).
Create an 'event' memory candidate for such past occurrences even if the date is only implicit, and include the resolved date in the memory content.

candidates.solves: Construction failed because a past event described only as 'last year' was not extracted, so no event memory was created. This is a recurring failure for relative time expressions, which are easy to skip when no explicit date appears. This Skill applies whenever a message with a timestamp contains a relative time phrase and a past event should be stored; it does not apply to messages without timestamps or to general statements lacking a time reference.

payload.name: Preserve-cumulative-event-counts
payload.description: When a message reports a new event in a countable series (e.g., second, fourth, final win/achievement), add a distinct event memory instead of updating or overwriting an earlier event memory.
content: During candidate extraction, when a message describes another occurrence in an ongoing countable series for the same person (e.g., a second, fourth, or final tournament win), extract it as a new event candidate; do not treat it as an update to an earlier event memory just because it is more recent.

During CRUD decisions, preserve prior discrete event memories when adding a new series occurrence; only UPDATE or ENRICH a memory when the new content genuinely refines that same occurrence, never when it describes a different instance. If the session implies a cumulative total, create or update a separate concise summary memory (e.g., 'has won N tournaments') without deleting individual event records.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: an UPDATE replaced Nate's first tournament win with his fourth, losing the cumulative count. Abstract mechanism: a new occurrence in a countable series was treated as a replacement for an older occurrence. Applies whenever future sessions mention sequential achievements/events (wins, awards, milestones) and counts must be preserved. Boundary: does not apply to enriching the same single event with additional details.

payload.name: Preserve distinct event instances on update
payload.description: When updating a memory, if the new message describes a different occurrence of a similar event (different ordinal, time, or instance), do not overwrite the existing memory; add a new memory while preserving the old.
content: During CRUD update, before replacing an existing memory, check whether the incoming event is the same instance or a new instance of a repeated event type.
If the new event has a different ordinal (first, second, fourth, etc.), different date/time, or otherwise different occurrence context, treat it as a separate event.
Preserve the existing memory unchanged and ADD a new memory for the new event instance. Do not merge distinct instances into one memory by overwriting the old content.
Only overwrite or enrich an existing memory when the new information clearly refers to the exact same event instance already recorded.

candidates.solves: When new evidence describes another occurrence of a repeated event type (e.g., first vs. fourth win), the construction agent may overwrite an older memory with the later occurrence, erasing a question-answerable fact. This rule distinguishes event instances by ordinal, time, or context and preserves earlier memories by adding separate memories for new instances. It applies to any recurring event domain (tournaments, trips, jobs) during CRUD updates, not to enriching the same event instance.

payload.name: Preserve existing facts during memory updates
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing memory, keep all previously recorded facts that are not contradicted by new evidence; add new details instead of replacing the entire content.
content: Before applying UPDATE or MERGE to an existing memory, compare the proposed new content with the existing memory content.

Retain every existing fact that remains true and is not explicitly contradicted by the new message; if new evidence adds context or corrects a detail, revise only the affected portion and keep the rest.

If the new information describes a different aspect or event, prefer ADDing a new memory or enriching with an additional sentence; do not rewrite the memory so that previously supported claims disappear.
When an update would remove an earlier explicit statement, treat it as suspect and instead produce content that includes both the old and new facts.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause was an UPDATE that rewrote a memory's content based on a later message and erased a previously captured fact that the later message did not contradict. This abstract failure occurs whenever a construction agent treats a later message as a replacement for the whole memory instead of as incremental enrichment. The rule applies to future UPDATE/MERGE decisions on any topic: preserve all non-contradicted existing facts, add new details, and only drop information explicitly invalidated by the new evidence.

payload.name: Preserve existing facts when updating memories
payload.description: When a new message describes a different event or topic than an existing memory, keep the original content and ADD or MERGE rather than overwriting.
content: Before updating an existing memory, compare the new message's event/topic with the stored memory's event/topic.
If they differ, do not replace the existing memory; create a new memory for the new facts or merge by appending while retaining the original content.
Preserve previously stored durable facts unless the new message explicitly contradicts them.

candidates.solves: A later construction update can overwrite a correctly stored memory with unrelated facts from a new message, deleting previously captured durable claims. The rule separates distinct events/topics: before replacing an existing memory, check whether the new facts concern the same event/topic; if not, add a separate memory or merge while preserving original content. It does not apply when the new message directly contradicts the old memory, in which case updating is appropriate.

payload.name: PreservePriorFactsOnMemoryUpdate
payload.description: When updating an existing memory with new details about the same subject, preserve previously stored facts unless directly contradicted by the new evidence.
content: During UPDATE operations on an existing memory, merge the new information into the existing content instead of replacing the whole memory. Keep all prior facts that are not explicitly contradicted by the new message. If a fact is genuinely contradicted, remove only that fact and update it with the corrected value; retain all other existing facts.

candidates.solves: When an UPDATE rewrites an existing memory using only the newest message's details, earlier true facts about the same subject can be silently dropped. The reusable rule is to treat memory updates as merges: preserve prior facts unless directly contradicted by new evidence, and replace or remove only the superseded portion. This applies whenever a later message enriches or corrects an already-stored profile, preference, or entity memory.

payload.name: Preserve event date during enrichment updates
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing event memory with new information, if the new message does not explicitly restate or change the event date, keep the original world_start unchanged.
content: Before applying an UPDATE/MERGE to an event memory, check whether the triggering message explicitly provides a new date for the same event.
If the new message only adds related context or a separate event, do not change the original world_start; preserve the date already supported by earlier evidence.
When merging multiple events into one memory, retain each event's original date rather than assigning the latest message time to all contained events.

candidates.solves: When a later message enriches an existing event memory but does not explicitly change the event's date, the Construction Agent must not overwrite the original world_start with the later message timestamp. The diagnosed failure changed an originally correct launch date during an unrelated enrichment update, so future updates should preserve the existing temporal anchor unless the new evidence explicitly revises it.

payload.name: Fact-preserving merge for new activity candidates
payload.description: When a construction decision would MERGE a candidate event into an existing memory and the candidate introduces a new activity, class, course, or group, use fact-preserving merge that keeps every distinct fact from both sides.
content: During the decision stage, before applying MERGE to a candidate, compare the candidate's content against the proposed merged content. If any distinct fact from the candidate (such as enrolling in a class, course, workshop, or group) is absent from the merged result, preserve it: either append that fact explicitly to the merged memory or ADD the candidate as a separate memory.

When a MERGE changes an existing memory's object/activity label to the candidate's new label, verify the new activity itself appears in the resulting content. Changing only the label while keeping old details is not enough and loses the candidate fact.

candidates.solves: Construction decisions that MERGE a candidate describing a new event or activity into an existing memory can silently drop the candidate's core fact, as happened when an agility-class candidate was merged into a hiking/dog-park memory and the class was absent from the merged content. The abstract failure is merging without fact preservation. This rule applies whenever a future candidate introduces a distinct event/activity/class/course/group and the decision is to merge it with a broader existing memory; it ensures no durable fact is lost.

payload.name: Preserve distinct event facts during updates
payload.description: When a later user message describes an event or plan different from the primary activity in an existing memory, do not overwrite the memory's object_text or core content; create a new memory or append while preserving the old fact.
content: When an incoming message mentions a new event or plan for a subject, check whether an existing event memory already records a different primary activity. If the activities are distinct, do not overwrite the memory's object_text or remove its core content; instead create a new event/plan memory or append the new fact while preserving the old one.

During candidate extraction, treat each explicitly distinct activity or plan as its own event candidate with its own timing and source, even when the same subject already appears in earlier memories; do not collapse them into a single mutable summary.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause was an UPDATE that replaced a memory's object_text ('agility classes') with a later planned activity ('stroll'), erasing a previously extracted fact. The abstract failure mechanism is conflating a newly mentioned distinct activity with an existing memory and letting the update overwrite the memory's central topic. The rule applies whenever a later message describes a different event or plan for a subject that already has a memory, preserving durable facts across construction.

payload.name: Preserve candidate facts when merging memories
payload.description: When a construction MERGE combines a new candidate with an existing memory, use the merged content to retain all distinct facts from the candidate, such as donation beneficiaries or organizations.
content: During construction CRUD, when applying a MERGE, compare candidate content with the existing memory and ensure every discrete factual assertion from the candidate appears in the new version.

If the candidate names a donation recipient, cause, organization, or similar affiliation, keep that fact in the merged memory; if the existing memory cannot hold it without losing other key facts, create or update a separate memory for that fact instead of dropping it.

candidates.solves: Construction MERGE decisions sometimes collapse a candidate into a related existing memory and accidentally drop a discrete fact that was present in the candidate (here, the donation recipient). Future questions may ask about that dropped fact, so the merged memory must preserve every distinct fact from the candidate. This applies only to CRUD merge operations on construction candidates, not to retrieval or answer generation, and does not require retaining non-factual wording or irrelevant details.

payload.name: Preserve distinct events during memory update
payload.description: When updating an existing event memory, apply this if the new message describes a different activity, time, or plan than the stored event, to avoid overwriting unrelated information.
content: Before applying an UPDATE to an existing event memory, compare the new message's activity, time, and subject with the stored content. If they describe different events, do not replace the stored content.

If the new information is a separate event, either create a new memory for it or merge it into the existing memory as additional context while preserving all previously recorded planned or occurred events.
When merging multiple events into one memory, keep each event's time and subject explicit so future retrieval can still find every relevant plan.

candidates.solves: Construction failed when a later UPDATE overwrote an existing planned event with a new, unrelated event, deleting the earlier fact. The abstract mechanism is treating any new event as a replacement of the target memory rather than recognizing it as a separate event. A rule that requires checking subject, time, and activity before UPDATE preserves coexisting events and transfers to any domain with multiple plans or activities for the same person or group.

payload.name: Preserve prior facts when updating memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new information, preserve all previously stored facts unless directly contradicted or superseded; if new details describe a separate event, keep both instead of overwriting.
content: Before applying UPDATE or MERGE, compare new evidence against existing memory content and retain every old fact that is not explicitly contradicted or superseded by the new message.
If the new information describes a different event, time period, or state of the world, do not overwrite older content; append it or create a separate memory so earlier facts remain available.
When changing world_start or state, still keep durable background facts that remain true, such as preferences, ongoing activities, and long-term care routines.

candidates.solves: When a new event or state is added to an existing memory, the update should not replace the entire memory and drop previously stored facts. The diagnosed failure occurred because an UPDATE to a memory about a beach trip replaced the content with a later knee-injury event, losing the beach fact. This rule abstracts that mechanism: during UPDATE/MERGE, preserve non-contradicted facts or split into separate memories. It applies to any future session where new evidence is recorded against an existing memory that contains multiple independent facts.

payload.name: Preserve unrelated plans during memory updates
payload.description: When updating a memory, if the incoming message introduces a different plan or event for the same subject, add a new memory instead of overwriting the existing one.
content: Before executing an UPDATE on an existing memory, compare the new evidence with the memory's current content. If they describe different plans, projects, events, or topics, do not overwrite the old memory; ADD a new memory for the new information and leave the existing memory unchanged.
When extracting candidates, treat distinct plans or events for the same subject as separate memories unless new evidence explicitly supersedes or corrects the earlier plan.
If a message only adds details to an existing plan, UPDATE or enrich that memory; if it introduces an unrelated activity, preserve the original and create a separate entry.

candidates.solves: A construction UPDATE can replace a prior correct memory with unrelated content when a later message mentions a different plan by the same person. This rule prevents loss of earlier evidence by requiring the agent to verify topical alignment before UPDATE and to ADD new distinct plans separately. Applies to any future update where new and old memory are not revisions of the same claim.

payload.name: Preserve prior facts when updating event memories
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing event memory with details from a later message, preserve all still-valid previously stored facts and avoid replacing the whole content with only the new activity.
content: During UPDATE or MERGE on an existing event memory, treat the existing content as preserved by default: keep every fact that remains true; never overwrite the entire content with only the new message's details.

When a later message describes a different activity or event than the memory currently stores, do not replace object_text/content with the new topic. Update only genuinely changed fields, or ADD a separate memory for the new event, so earlier facts remain retrievable.

candidates.solves: Construction agents can destroy previously captured facts when a later message triggers an UPDATE that rewrites an existing event memory with new activity details, making earlier claims unanswerable. This skill applies whenever one memory is updated or enriched from a new message; it requires preserving all still-valid existing facts and narrowing edits to genuinely changed fields, creating a new memory when the new event is distinct.

payload.name: Preserve old facts when updating an event memory
payload.description: When updating an existing event or state memory with facts from a new message, check whether the update would drop or overwrite previously stored durable facts from the same subject that are not contradicted or subsumed by the new content; preserve them by merging or splitting instead of replacing.
content: During the update stage, before applying an UPDATE, compare the target memory's current content with the new candidate facts from the triggering message.

If the new facts describe different events, states, preferences, or relationships than the old content and do not contradict or fully supersede it, do not overwrite the existing memory. Keep the old memory unchanged and add a separate new memory for the new facts, or merge them into a combined content that retains all distinct durable claims.

When a new message mentions an activity or emotion that elaborates on an existing memory's topic without invalidating the old statement, preserve the original claim and its reason/cause; do not let a newer activity replace an older fact merely because it is newer.

After any UPDATE or enrichment, verify that every true claim from the referenced prior memory version remains present in the resulting memory or another memory; if a previously stored fact disappears, restore it.

candidates.solves: When updating an existing memory from a new message, the agent may overwrite old durable facts. This Skill applies to UPDATE operations where new content does not contradict or subsume old content and the old facts remain true; preserve them by merging or splitting instead of replacing. It does not apply to DELETEs, corrections, or direct contradictions.

payload.name: Preserve specific facts when updating memories
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing memory with new information, retain all previously recorded specific facts that are not explicitly contradicted; merge rather than replace.
content: Before applying an UPDATE or enrichment to an existing memory, compare the existing content against new evidence and list existing factual details (e.g., specific type, exact date, duration) that are not contradicted; these must be kept.

When new information adds context but does not explicitly contradict an existing fact, preserve the original specific detail and add the new detail as supplemental, rather than overwriting the original with a paraphrase or inference.

Only change world_start or other temporal fields when new evidence explicitly revises the event date; resolve relative expressions like 'last week' from the message timestamp and match them to the existing timeframe.

candidates.solves: Updates to existing event memories often replace precise details (specific injury type, exact date) with broader paraphrases or inferred causes from later messages, losing answerable facts. This skill instructs construction agents to preserve uncontradicted specific facts when enriching, keeping event content and timing faithful to all evidence. Applies whenever a later message adds context to a previously stored event without explicitly negating earlier details.

payload.name: Preserve distinct events during memory updates
payload.description: When a later message describes an event that differs from an existing memory's date, outcome, or completion status, do not overwrite the existing event memory; keep it and add a separate memory for the new event.
content: Before updating an existing event memory, compare the new message with the stored content: if the event date, completion status, or core facts differ, the new message describes a distinct event. Do not overwrite the original memory; preserve it and create a separate memory for the new event if it is durable.
When extracting candidates, treat events with different dates or different outcomes as separate memories, even if they share the same subject and topic.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that an UPDATE overwrote a correct earlier event memory with a different later event, losing the original completion date and status. The abstract failure is conflating two distinct events during update/extraction by replacing rather than preserving older facts. This rule applies when a construction agent processes messages that reference the same subject but different temporal or outcome details; it guides the agent to keep distinct events separate instead of destructive overwrite.

payload.name: Preserve distinct events during memory updates
payload.description: When a new message describes an event related but temporally distinct from an existing memory, use ADD for the new event instead of UPDATE overwriting the old one.
content: When extracting a new event that is temporally distinct from an existing memory about the same subject, do not UPDATE the old memory's content or world_start to match the new event; instead ADD a new memory for the new event and leave the existing memory unchanged.

candidates.solves: Construction failures occur when an existing memory about an earlier event is overwritten by a later, distinct event during UPDATE, losing the original date and details. This rule prevents that by requiring temporally distinct events to be stored as separate memories rather than merging them into one. It applies to any subject with multiple related events at different times.

payload.name: Preserve existing dates when enriching memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new information, keep all original dates and factual details; do not let a new date replace or obscure the old one.
content: During UPDATE/MERGE of an existing memory, retain all original temporal details (explicit dates, relative times, world_start/world_end) in the updated memory; do not omit or overwrite them when adding new facts.
If the update adds a new dated event to the same memory, record both dates explicitly in the content unless one event genuinely supersedes the other.
Before finalizing an update, verify that every key fact and date from the prior memory version is still present and unambiguous in the new version.

candidates.solves: When enriching an existing memory with a new event or fact, update/merge operations can drop or obscure the original event's date, causing later questions about the earlier event to be only partially answerable. This rule preserves all existing temporal anchors and factual details during any UPDATE/MERGE that adds new information, so future retrieval can still resolve the original event's date. It applies whenever a memory is extended with a later event, but not when new information intentionally corrects or supersedes an old date.

payload.name: Preserve previous item when updating with a new instance
payload.description: When constructing memories and an existing memory stores one item (e.g., a book) but a later message mentions a different item in the same category, use this Skill before choosing UPDATE.
content: During extraction, when a message names a new item in a category (book, movie, game, hobby) and an existing memory already names a different item, emit the new item as an ADD candidate, not as an UPDATE/correction of the existing one, unless the speaker explicitly retracts or contradicts the earlier item.

During CRUD, if an existing 'currently reading/watching/using' memory describes a different item, preserve that old memory (close its world_end or keep it as a past event) and ADD the new item as a separate memory; use update_type correction only when the old memory is factually wrong.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: a new book mention was treated as a correction, so an UPDATE overwrote an old reading memory. The abstract failure is confusing an additional instance with a correction; when a new item in a category already has a stored item, preserve the prior fact and add the new item separately. Applies to multi-item categories (books, movies, hobbies); not when the speaker explicitly retracts or corrects the old fact.

operations.name: Preserve distinct events during memory updates
operations.description: When updating or merging an existing memory, if the new message describes a different event, activity, plan, or instance (different ordinal, date, or topic), do not overwrite the existing memory; ADD a new memory or merge while preserving all prior non-contradicted facts.
content: Before applying UPDATE or MERGE, compare the new message's event/activity/plan with the existing memory's content. If they describe different instances (different ordinal, date/time, completion status, or topic), do not overwrite the existing memory; ADD a new memory for the new instance and leave the old memory unchanged.

When new information enriches the same event instance, preserve all previously stored facts that are not explicitly contradicted; merge new details into the existing content instead of replacing the whole memory.

If a MERGE combines a candidate with an existing memory, ensure every distinct fact from the candidate (e.g., new activity, donation recipient, date) appears in the merged content; if it cannot be retained without losing other key facts, create a separate memory for that fact.
Do not change world_start or other temporal fields during enrichment unless the new message explicitly revises the date of the same event; preserve original dates and details.
